$comment: CAP: 12 prose entries across expected_shape · read_this_way · suspicious_if ·
blind_spots · decisions · review_notes · expected · known_normal · known_bad ·
The cap is checked over this file by step-validate fast invariant #45 (NOTES-CAP). When a 13th wants in
there are exactly two legal resolutions: PROMOTE it to a check, or DELETE it.
There is no overflow file and no overflow block.
`fences` is a RECORD block, not prose — it is not counted against the cap. It
lives here because the descriptor schema's root is additionalProperties:false

expected_shape.what: Every run of this step LOADS. There is no staleness gate — no HEAD/ETag probe, no content hash, no local-shapefile short-circuit (the argv/local-path override and the `data/3d-massing-wgs84/` cache were retired per Spec 124 R-AZ, M-D10) — so an unchanged source reads inserted 0 / updated 0 and the audit table is the post-write counter block plus the declared check rows, never a skip. M-D3 is the one forced diff: the legacy read updated 4 on every unchanged run (cross-batch self-overwrite of duplicate geometry-hash keys, MEASURED runs 1285/1359/1400/1478); the runner dedupes the whole set last-wins, so the data is identical and updated goes 4 → 0.

constants.what: `'hash_'` + the 12 md5 hex chars are the KEY FORMAT, not a tunable: massing's coerceKey builds source_id as 'hash_' + md5(JSON.stringify(geometry)).slice(0,12) because the DBF carries no OBJECTID/ID. Changing either the prefix or the 12 truncation RE-KEYS the table — every one of 427,077 rows gets a new source_id and the old row is never retracted (class A, no re-key path), so the table would double. It is a storage-format constant in compute, named here with why (parcels D3 precedent). Likewise `* 100 / 100` (2 dp on max_height_m / min_height_m / elev_z) and `* 10000000 / 10000000` (1e-7 on the centroid lat/lng) are STORAGE-FORMAT constants inside shapeRecord, each re-stating what the column stores. The unit constant `10.7639104167` (m2 → ft2) and the area `scale:2` live in scripts/lib/step/write.js and the descriptor respectively (prerequisite 0u), NOT as logic variables: an admin knob over a unit conversion would silently rewrite every stored row rather than change a bound (the parcels D3 ruling).

read_this_way.what: `duplicate_key_count` ~1,107 is NORMAL, not a defect. The source has no id property, so source_id is md5(geometry) and identical geometries collide: the P-M probe measured 961 duplicate-geometry groups carrying 1,107 extra rows (428,184 − 427,077), of which only 28 groups differ in attributes. The step resolves duplicates LAST-wins by file order (the compute's dedupeBySourceId keeps the last feature per source_id before the upsert — M-D3, the same rule the legacy within-batch Map dedupe applied), so the surviving row is the last occurrence's — a duplicate split across two batches resolves the same way it always did. A non-zero count here is the source's own redundancy, not a run failure.

known_normal.what: `invalid_geometry_stored` ~17 is NORMAL. The step declares geometry_repair:"none" (M-D2, legacy parity — the legacy stored 17 invalid geometries unrepaired rather than run ST_MakeValid), so a carried row whose geometry is invalid is stored as-is and counted under acquired.invalid_geometry_stored (the Fold PB-3 library counter, goldens-neutral). The count is DESCRIPTIVE (INFO, never gates). It is ~17 on the measured input and is not a signal to add repair: F1 (flip to make_valid for new rows) is a separate post-conversion commit with its own RED→GREEN, deliberately not folded here.

decisions.what: The S2–S5 key-format auto-cleanup (detect a source_id strategy change and DELETE the mismatched rows + VACUUM) is RETIRED, not carried: it is dead on the measured input (0 non-`hash_` rows) and structurally unreachable after prerequisite 0s, because the converted coerceKey derives the key from geometry ALONE and ignores every DBF property — a publisher adding OBJECTID can no longer re-key the table (M-D1). Detection is preserved as the DECLARED invariant `building_footprints_foreign_key_space_rows` (FAIL if > 0); remediation is a RUNBOOK ACTION, never an automatic DELETE.

measured.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM building_footprints WHERE source_id NOT LIKE 'hash_%'

decisions.why: A non-zero count means a key re-format happened, and the fix is an operator decision — parcel_buildings.building_id carries an FK to building_footprints.id with NO cascade, so an automatic DELETE would either fail on the FK or, with a cascade added casually, silently drop 520,492 links. The run must FAIL loudly and hand the operator a runbook, not guess.

suspicious_if.what: `features_read` < 400,000 is a WARN (the shared sources_building_footprints_floor, value 400000 — the catastrophic-load detector, WARN-not-FAIL as the legacy read it). A `records_new` SPIKE on an unchanged CKAN sha256 is the more specific alarm: the source bytes did not move, so a sudden insert burst means the KEY FORMAT changed (the md5 input or the prefix moved), which re-keys every row into a fresh insert rather than an update — exactly the `building_footprints_foreign_key_space_rows` invariant's failure mode seen from the write side.

blind_spots.what: Two silent blind spots, both carried verbatim. (1) `geom` and the two area columns are INSERT-ONLY (the `geometry` jsonb IS updated): they are seeded at INSERT and NEVER recomputed on an update, exactly as the legacy area SET-omission (WF2 #C 2026-05-09) and the `WHERE geom IS NULL` pass did, so stored values can differ from a fresh re-derivation by float noise and the step never heals them (M-D8: 3,850 geoms by <= 1.42e-14 deg, 361 sqm / 3,868 sqft area rows by <= 0.01). (2) `elev_z` and `estimated_stories` are NOT guard columns (M-D4): a source change that moves only those is never written and nothing in the audit table shows it; F2 widens the guard post-cutover with its own RED fixture.

limitations.what: M-D5 — a changed building leaves its OLD row behind. source_id is a geometry hash and the class-A upsert has retract:"none", so when a building's geometry changes the new geometry is a NEW key (a fresh insert) and the previous key's row is never deleted; it stays in `building_footprints` forever and is still linkable by link_massing. The orphan count is 0 today (the P-M `--db` key diff found db_keys_absent_from_file = 0, file_keys_absent_from_db = 0), so the defect is latent/structural rather than presently manifest, but it is not closed here: retraction needs an FK/cascade design co-owned with link_massing (parcel_buildings.building_id has no cascade) and is filed in review_followups.

fences.const: the WF2 #C 2026-05-09 area SET-omission survives as insert_only
fences.value: columns footprint_area_sqm / footprint_area_sqft declared written:"insert_only" with derived_from_geometry {measure:"geodesic_area", unit:"m2"|"ft2", scale:2} (prerequisite 0u); the generated upsert's SET clause names neither column
fences.incident: WF2 #C 2026-05-09: the area pair is OMITTED from the upsert SET on purpose. If it were included, EXCLUDED would carry the freshly-derived value and OVERWRITE every existing row's stored area on a re-load — opening a window where compute-cost-estimates.js (advisory lock 83, independent of lock 56) reads a mid-flight value and takes the wrong GFA path. insert_only keeps the pair out of SET and the guard; the value is seeded at INSERT only, from the legacy S7 ST_Area(…::geography) expression.

fences.const: the S8 geom transform is 3857 → 4326 with geometry_repair:"none"
fences.value: outputs.writes[0].columns geom written:"insert_only", bind:"wkb_geometry", geometry_srid:3857; descriptor geometry_repair:"none"
fences.incident: WF3 2026-06-10: link_massing's PostGIS fast path (ST_Contains(bf.geom, parcel_centroid_4326)) needs geom populated in WGS84, but migrations 065/098 only ST_SetSRID'd without transforming, so the legacy added an explicit ST_Transform(…, 3857), 4326). geometry_repair:"none" stops the library from slipping ST_MakeValid in (massing is the FIRST consumer of the "none" arm; its 17 invalid geometries stay unrepaired, M-D2). The library polygon arm also skips its ST_Multi normalisation under "none" (0t follow-on, 2026-09-27, plan SF-2), so a new Polygon row is stored POLYGON exactly as the legacy stored it.

fences.const: Pipeline Rehab P2 (2026-08-03) — the mkdir-before-download is retired with downloadFile
fences.value: acquisition is the runner's acquire.js (download + extractArchive, format:"shapefile_zip"); acquire.js owns mkdtemp
fences.incident: The 2026-08-03 mkdir fix existed because the legacy downloadFile opened its write stream into the gitignored data/ dir, which does not exist on a fresh CI checkout, BEFORE the loader's only mkdirSync ran — a fresh runner crashed on the download. The converted step never touches data/: the local cache is retired (M-D10) and acquire.js's mkdtemp owns the temp dir, so the ordering hazard cannot recur. src/tests/sources-loader-mkdir.logic.test.ts:40's listing of load-massing.js is removed with the why.

fences.const: the CKAN resource id in ZIP_URL rotates; the durable fix is NOT in this conversion
fences.value: inputs.reads.externals[].url carries the current resource id as data; the package_show resolution stays a review_followups item
fences.incident: The dataset id is stable but the CKAN resource id is not: the previous id 404'd on 2026-08-03 (run 30842232783, 86 min into the chain) after a re-registration, while the filename part was unchanged. Because the converted step re-fetches from CKAN every run (staleness.trigger "none": no pre-acquisition gate, and acquire.js downloads into a per-run temp root it removes, so no local extract survives between runs — M-D10), a rotation now fails AFTER the download attempt rather than being masked by a stale local extract. Durable fix — resolve the newest resource at runtime via CKAN package_show instead of hardcoding — was filed 2026-08-03 and remains a separate change, not folded here.
